So my usual [manual transmission] car for the past six months has one of those handy [auto-hold electronic brakes](  If you press the brake when or until the car stops moving, it holds you there until you accelerate away again.

This week the car's been in the bodyshop after someone hit it while parked at my flat, and I've got a Fiesta to use instead.  Great, I used to have one, it feels familiar.

This evening I came back, at the end of a long day, to find a nice big parking space outside the flat, it could probably just fit two cars.  I quickly reverse into it, happy to be able to park nearby, and decide to park at the slightly closer end which is at the top of a slight incline.  I listen to the end of the U2 track on the radio, turn off the engine and hop out.

I get one foot out, stand up, and put one hand on the door to close it.  It feels lighter than usual.

I turn around to see the car accelerating away, down towards a little black Clio.  I've never moved so fast as I did then - dropped my things, jumped back into the car, and yanked the handbrake up as hard as I could just before it ended up in the back of the next parked car.

I don't think I could have faced explaining how I crashed into my neighbour's car, while my own car was being repaired for parking damage!  Looking forward to the return of my 21st century technologies.

TLDR; not all cars automatically brake for you

Hi there!

I am moving to Seattle in August and need a place to live... Unfortunately I have to leave the country for July, and it looks like I only have this week to travel to Seattle and settle on an apartment for August and beyond.

I have been doing a lot of online research but a lot of listings on Craig's List around the area I want to live in seem to be apartment complexes, and most of them have really bad reviews on Yelp... I have never been to Seattle, and I really need a local's help, so I decided to post on Reddit, see if anyone is willing to help a sister out.

Any realtors on here who is willing to show me some apartments this week and help me settle on one? I will provide the details once we get in touch.

tl;dr: moving to Seattle in a short notice, need a place to live. Internet search isn't doing me well. Help!

Edit: Found a realtor on yelp who is willing to help me out. The side bare gave me a good idea of where I should be looking. I am looking to live around Seattle University (going to graduate school there), so First Hill or Capital Hill, or Central District. I'm looking for a one-bed, size isn't important except I want a decent-sized kitchen. $1500 is my maximum.

I live in Somerville MA (about a mile outside Boston)

Looking to try a business selling specialty food products. I've posted about this a while ago but I'm now able to spend the money. I have two products right now (see end for long descriptions).

My idea is to make a test batch of each product, and get some of my friends and family together, have food & drinks and obviously feature my products. Tell them a little about my ideas, and give them some to take home, and some to give to a friend. This is not to try raising money. I just want to get some feedback and get some branded products in their hands to.

I really want to concentrate on the branding and marketing of these. Simple, sophisticated design. I'm a capable designer and my brother is a professional web designer. Trying to capitalize on the hipster & foodie crowd. There's a lot of people in my area who appreciate specialty (bakeries, butchers, small ethnic food shops, fish shops, etc). There's also a great deal of Portuguese around here, in southern MA, and in RI, which is pertinent to the marketing of one of my products.

* One is a portuguese hot pepper sauce called pimenta moida. My grandmother's recipe. It's a crushed sauce, not really a tabasco or siracha. Since it's crushed it's more of a pulverized relish. And it has a distinct vinegary/saltiness. great on fish or sandwiches. The selling point with mine is that it's a cleaner sauce. Most products have a lot of seeds because they just crush the entire pepper without deseeding.

* The second is a great pepper jelly my mother makes. Great with cheese and crackers.



**TL;DR**

Want to start a company to sell food products and host a party some of my friends/fam to show them what I plan to sell (NOT TO GET MONEY)

As a developer I'd like to clear something up; unless its an indie studio we basically have no say on what we make. If the 'business' people (wannabe wolfs of wallstreet w.w.w.) say do it we do it with the tools given to us by the device manufacturers and limitations put in place by everybody but us. I've long stopped making games but thats how it is basically.

Now on the other hand theres studios like Mojang(makers of minecraft) where the developer controlled how the game was done because its his company and hes the one making the product and was limited only by the power of the pc.

***tl;dr: Developers and publishers are different aspects of the gaming business. E.g. Ubisoft and Mojang arent reigned over the same way.***
